data.gender_notes: Malekai is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Malekai is derived from the Hebrew word mālāk, which means 'my angel'. This name is often associated with the biblical figure Malachi, which means 'my messenger'. Malekai is a powerful name for a boy, symbolizing protection, guidance, and divine intervention. The name Malekai carries the meaning “My angel” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Malekai usually hope their child will grow to embody my angel and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the presence and guidance of angels in our lives.
data.etymology: Malekai belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My angel.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Malekai total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: מלקאי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מלקאי הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'שליח אלוהים' או 'קריין מלך'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'מלק' שפירושו 'מלך' ו'אי' שפירושו 'אלוהים' או 'אלהים'. השם מלקאי מופיע בספר מלאכי שבתנך, שם מלאכי הוא נביא ששלח אלוהים לדבר אל עם ישראל.

in_greek.name: Μαλαχίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Μαλαχίας είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος מלקאי. Στη Βίβλο, ο Μαλαχίας ήταν προφήτης που στάλθηκε από τον Θεό για να μιλήσει στον λαό του Ισραήλ. Το όνομα Μαλαχίας σημαίνει 'αγγελος του Θεου' ή 'αγγελος του Κυρίου'.

in_latin.name: Malachias
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Malachias derivatur ex hebraico מלקאי, quod significat 'angelus Dei' vel 'messenger of God'. In Ecclesia primitiva, Malachias fuit propheta qui missus est a Deo ad populum Israel.

in_english.name: Malekai
in_english.meaning: Messenger of God or Angel of the Lord
in_english.long_meaning: The name Malekai is derived from the Hebrew name מלקאי (Malakai), which means 'messenger of God' or 'angel of the Lord'. It is associated with the prophet Malachi in the Old Testament, who was sent by God to speak to the Israelites. The name has been adopted in various Christian traditions and is often given to boys born into Christian families.

pronunciation.biblical: מלקאי (pronounced as mal-ˈkaɪ in a biblical Hebrew context)

historical_references.reference: Malekai, a medieval Hebrew name believed to be derived from the Hebrew word 'malak' meaning 'messenger'. It was used by the Jewish community in medieval Europe as a personal name for boys. This name was later adopted by some Christians, particularly in the Iberian Peninsula, during the late Middle Ages.

Malekai, a name mentioned in various medieval legends and folktales, often associated with miracles or supernatural events. In one such story, a knight named Malekai is said to have rescued a poor woman from a dragon, converting her to Christianity in the process. Another legend tells of a hermit named Malekai who lived in a cave and was visited by a pilgrim, offering him food and shelter. These stories served to popularize the name among Christians.
